A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bridge research work. Their complete 16-page documents, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across three language models and seven math benchmarks, with generation-scaling, warm-up, feature-contribution, and architectural-placement analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original math experiments and appendix results, and additionally reports evaluations on five other benchmarks and output-stability measurements.

M1.justification: The masked attention across simultaneous generations, block placement, positional-encoding omission, SFT warm-up, and GRPO objective remain unchanged. Shortened mathematical subscripts and the suggestion of future RLHF applications do not change the implemented method.

E1.justification: Section 4.1.3 and new Table 2 substantially broaden evaluation beyond the original seven math benchmarks by adding XSum and CNN/DailyMail summarization, GPQA, ZebraLogic, and Countdown. GSM8K warm-up and DeepScaleR training coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain the original model, RLVR only, and the parameter-matched MLP baseline P-Match. V2 extends this same comparator set to its new benchmarks and output-stability analysis; newly cited related methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.3 increases responses per competition-math problem from 16 to 32, also reflected in the width-analysis table. MATH-500 retains four responses. New experiments introduce ROUGE-1 evaluation, pairwise BERTScore F1, and response-score variance measurements, while training, checkpoint selection, temperature, and generation widths remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3.5 and Table 5 add a focused DS-Qwen-7B analysis of output similarity on MATH-500 and response-quality variation on summarization tasks. These examine possible output collapse and consistency. Existing width, length, warm-up, feature-norm, and Appendix D placement analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 4 and 5 newly include error bars, and Table 5 adds within-prompt ROUGE-1 variance estimates. The PDFs do not define the new error bars or disclose additional training runs or seeds. Response-score variance measures output dispersion rather than uncertainty across independently trained models.

E6.justification: V2 revises competition-math results in Table 1, the width table, and Figures 4–5, and adds substantial results in Tables 2 and 5. For example, Bridge's DS-Qwen-7B average changes from 39.83 to 39.40 under the larger response budget, retaining the best average ranking; this is not a same-setting performance decline. Length, warm-up, feature-norm, and appendix placement results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The attention and training equations, conditional-independence statements, Pass@k and G-Pass definitions, and Appendix C argument about advantages are retained. Changes from Attn/Bridge subscripts to A/B and more compact equation formatting are mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract reduces the headline relative RLVR improvement from up to 50% to 39%. The introduction expands the claimed empirical support from seven math benchmarks to seven math and five additional benchmarks. The central architectural contribution, parameter overhead, and generation-width claims remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new BERTScore measurements as slight similarity growth without output collapse, and lower ROUGE variance as more consistent quality. It also asserts preservation of non-math performance after math-only training and suggests RLHF applicability. The blanket non-degradation interpretation exceeds what all Table 2 point estimates support.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, training hyperparameters, parameter counts, and pseudocode remain substantively unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices A, B, and E. Renaming 'Mixing heads' and 'Mixing group size' to 'Heads' and 'Generation width' adds no new settings. No new implementation or resource-access instructions are provided.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds Macfarlane et al. (2025), and the bibliography adds sources for the new benchmarks, ROUGE, and BERTScore. Existing parallel-synthesis references are retained, as is the positioning around producing multiple interdependent outputs rather than aggregating parallel computation into one output.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized abstract, introduction, related-work, and explanatory edits; adds the Output Stability subsection and a work-at-Meta author note; and shortens mathematical notation. The main section sequence, narrative organization, and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 2 and 5, redraws Figure 4 with solid bars and error bars, and updates Figure 5's error bars and axis scale. Several displays move as text reflows, including Table 1 and Figure 7. The overall layout and Figures 1–3, 6, and 7 are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The added transfer evaluations and output-similarity/variance diagnostics strengthen empirical support for useful interdependent response sets beyond v1's math-only evidence. These gains are limited by undefined error bars and overbroad interpretation: the new 'no degradation' statement overlooks, for example, DS-Llama-8B CNN/DailyMail ROUGE-1 of 22.64 versus 23.84 for the original model.
